correctness.rationale: The primary source proves an independent parent-choice construction. Multiplying a vector probability by lambda^(number of roots) yields independent weighted choices and exactly preserves each fixed-root-count conditional law. Under the tilt the root count has linear mean/positive variance and a Fourier-provable local CLT. The exact component-size mean recursion is a stable triangular Euler scheme, solved by a time-inhomogeneous Yule geometric kernel. Bounded differences give O(exp(-cn)) tails, surviving the O(n^-1/2) conditioning probability. The exact mass identities and truncation prove the full weighted-l1 theorem. Independently implemented finite rational enumeration and integral/recurrence checks pass 170 assertions.

value.rationale: The original forest model has an explicitly known count of tree components but lacks a closed full partition law. A fixed atypical count of order alpha*n is a natural conditioning test of dependence between count and sizes. The result characterizes all finite sizes simultaneously, supplies both component-biased and vertex-biased conditional laws in total variation, and expresses their deformation through an explicit uniquely calibrated Yule mixture. The claim is an infinite family of nontrivial rare-event conditional laws, not a textbook normalization or a known-table recomputation.
